analysis:
The PR adds a GPT-OSS/Harmony stop-string scope, a functional change to output semantics rather than to any trust boundary. GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFix.finalChannelStopScope (GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFixes.swift:45-47) defines an opener of `<|channel|>final` with `<|message|>` as openerEnd, and closers `<|end|>`, `<|return|>`, `<|call|>` and `<|start|>`. ChatTemplateFixes.stopStringScope (ChatTemplateFixes.swift:136-139) and ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope return this scope only when the model hint contains gpt-oss. EngineV2SlotFactory.swift:574 passes it to EngineV2Factory.makeBridge. Tests cover the bridge matching and request translation.

Security review: no new network, file or key surface, and no changes to attestation, encryption, authorization, the prefix cache (T-041) or the SSD cache. Stop strings are still client-supplied and are matched against provider-generated text, so a malicious consumer (ADV-002) gains nothing new. Consumers could already stop generation with their own stop strings, and the scope only narrows where matching applies. Stop-string matching on model output is already within the consumer's control; the scope neither exposes data nor bypasses billing.

Remaining unverified: the implementations of CBv2StopStringScope and EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence/EngineV2Translation (in MLXLMCommon or other unchanged files, not supplied). Possible issues there include unbounded scanning cost on adversarially long outputs, or an output-length-limit bypass. These are a DoS/performance concern in unseen code, not evidenced by this diff. The changes in this batch themselves introduce no concrete regression. The EngineV2Bridge changes that consume the scope are not in the supplied units, so the integration pass should check them if available.
